_typeNote: Raised across the board on 2026-07-26. A slide is looked at for about a second, at roughly 400px wide, by a thumb already moving. Body copy under 46px on a 1080px canvas is a document, not a poster; the published contrast slide sat at 48px inside panels filling 45% of the frame and read as empty. These minimums are floors the auto-fitter may not go under, not targets.
_coverageNote: Share of the space a layout gave the type that the type must actually occupy, per archetype. A slide whose text sits in a small island inside a large void reads as a template someone forgot to finish: the published contrast slide that started this rewrite measured 0.38 against the 0.80 floor it now has. Calibrated 2026-07-26 against a full re-render, with headroom: hook 0.68 measured against a 0.50 floor, stat 0.78 against 0.60, content 1.09 against 0.75, contrast 1.00 against 0.80. `quote` and `cta` are picture-led by design, their type is deliberately a short block low in the frame, and their floors are set low enough to catch only an empty slide.
_paletteNote: One account, not one post. Four covers side by side on the profile grid were indistinguishable: same cold blue-teal, same cyan accent, same layout. Two causes, both mine — the .tint layer recoloured every photograph toward the accent with mix-blend-mode:color, and every generated prompt asked for cold blue light. The typeface, the black ground and the handle are what make this one account; the accent is what makes each post a different one. Chosen by the story's mood, which the post already declares. The accent alone was not enough: three of four posts declared mood `tension`, so the grid stayed one colour. The mood therefore sets the light of the PICTURE too — every illustration prompt carries its palette's `light` phrase — because what makes two covers look alike is the photograph, not the eight per cent of accent sitting on top of it.

steady.why: the house colour, cold and neutral
steady.light: cold cyan light and near-black shadow

tension.why: amber: something broke, or someone was hurt
tension.light: warm amber light against deep shadow

wonder.why: violet: something became possible that was not
wonder.light: violet dusk light and soft haze
